signer: An address that must approve a transaction with a signature.
program: An on-chain Solana executable account that processes instructions.
instruction: A single command inside a Solana transaction sent to a program.
SPL token: A token using Solana's standard token program (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA).
token account: An account that holds a specific token for a wallet owner.
associated token account: The standard token account address for a wallet and token mint pair, derived deterministically.
authority: An address with permission to control a token account, mint, or delegate setting.
delegate: An address authorized to spend tokens from a token account up to a set limit without further approval.
approval: A permission (SPL Token Approve instruction) that lets another address move tokens from your account up to the approved amount.
mint: The token identifier that defines a specific SPL token or NFT collection/item.
transfer: A movement of SOL, tokens, or NFTs between accounts.
memo: Optional text attached to a Solana transaction, often used for exchange deposits or tagging.
compute budget: Instructions that tune compute units or priority fees for a transaction.
SetAuthority: An SPL Token instruction that permanently changes the owner or freeze authority of a token account or mint. Signing this hands control to another address.
CloseAccount: An SPL Token instruction that closes a token account and sends its lamport balance to a specified destination. If the destination is an attacker, all remaining tokens are lost.
InitializeAccount: An SPL Token instruction that creates a new token account for a given mint and owner.
createAccount: A System Program instruction that allocates space on-chain and funds a new account with SOL for rent. Often the first step in creating a token account.
versioned transaction: A transaction format (version 0+) that supports Address Lookup Tables, allowing more accounts per transaction. Can obscure the full list of accounts involved.
address lookup table (ALT): An on-chain table of account addresses referenced by versioned transactions. Reduces transaction size but can hide the real accounts being acted on until fully resolved.
inner instruction: An instruction invoked by a program during execution (CPI — Cross-Program Invocation), not directly by the user. Inner instructions can perform token transfers or approvals that are not visible in the top-level instruction list.
CPI (Cross-Program Invocation): When one Solana program calls another during execution. Drainer contracts use CPI to invoke token approvals or transfers invisibly inside a seemingly benign outer instruction.
rent: A small SOL fee required to keep an account alive on-chain. Accounts below the rent-exempt threshold may be garbage-collected.
lamport: The smallest unit of SOL. 1 SOL = 1,000,000,000 lamports.
nonce account: A special account that enables durable transactions by replacing the recent blockhash with an off-chain nonce. Can be used to pre-authorize transactions that execute later.
freeze authority: An authority that can freeze a token account, preventing transfers. If an attacker holds the freeze authority, they can lock your tokens.
token-2022 (Token Extensions): An upgraded SPL token program supporting extensions like transfer fees, confidential transfers, and interest-bearing tokens. Transactions involving Token-2022 accounts may have additional hidden behaviors.
System Program: The core Solana program (11111111111111111111111111111111) that handles SOL transfers, account creation, and ownership changes.
ComputeBudget: A program that sets priority fees and compute unit limits. Presence alone is not risky, but very high priority fees may indicate bot activity.
